output.summary: KEP-2896 proposes publishing OpenAPI v3 for Kubernetes types at /openapi/v3/apis/{group}/{version}, one spec per group-version instead of one aggregated spec, with the aggregated document no longer served at /openapi/v3. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: OpenAPI v2 conversion strips information from CRD schemas (oneOf, anyOf, nullable, default), and one monolithic aggregated spec forces clients to re-download everything on any change. Splitting by group-version makes the published v3 lossless and cheaper to fetch. Reviewers raised concerns about incomplete v3 data during transition, which led to making v2->v3 conversion a beta requirement.

alternatives.option: Keep a separately maintained, hand-written OpenAPI v3 spec as source of truth instead of generating from Go types
alternatives.why_not: Maintainers said it was out of scope for this KEP and that hand-written OpenAPI as source of truth had little chance of agreement; the KEP is about publishing the spec via a new endpoint.

alternatives.option: Aggregate by group only instead of group-version
alternatives.why_not: Splitting by group-version was chosen because it removes the aggregation step; the group-only split was only about 30% smaller in total size, which was judged less important.

alternatives.option: For aggregated apiservers, convert v2 to v3 and publish a lossy v3 schema
alternatives.why_not: Discussed by jefftree as an alternative; the sources do not state a final rejection rationale, but the v2->v3 conversion was later accepted as a beta requirement with the caveat that it is ugly but feasible.

alternatives.option: Drop v3 publishing for old apiservers until upgraded (version skew handling)
alternatives.why_not: This was the position adopted in the version-skew section, so it is not an alternative that was rejected; it is noted as the chosen handling for skew.

evidence.quote: The proposal is to publish OpenAPI v3 schemas at the `/openapi/v3/apis/{group}/{version}` endpoint for all resources.
There are a couple of important fields part of the CRD structural schema that are stripped when we publish v2: `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `nullable`, `default`.
let's adopt splitting by group-version given the advantages of a omitting an aggregation step with group-version
v2->v3 is fine as a beta requirement. We will attempt that. I think it is ugly, but feasible.
I am pretty sure, however, that there's little chance people would agree to hand-write OpenAPI and make that the source of truth.
